Posted April 17, 2002

(MarijuanaNews note: This excerpt from an article in The Cincinnati Enquirer

The first is rah-rah uncritical cheering for even the most cynical efforts to manipulate children using patriotism. The end justifies the means.

The second feature is the civic boosterism. It cheerfully reports that " The conference will bring $4.2 million into the local economy. " Isn't that nice. Cincinnatti is for sale? Simple-minded boosterism of this sort, supporting local DARE programs, for example, are a just a part of doing business for newspapers.

Finally, it shows a complete unwillingness to question even the most absurd statements by an authority figure. Simple common sense observation should tell anyone that cannabis is NOT " two-thirds of the addiction problem in America today. "

But if The Cincinnati Enquirer were to question anything the prohibitionists say, the city might not be able to prostitute itself for $4.2 million next year. Worse, the paper might encourage critical thinking by its readers and that would be a threat to the paper itself.)

Excerpted from:
US Drug Chief Waves The Flag

Thousands Attend International Conference In Cincinnati.

The Cincinnati Enquirer

By Cindy Kranz
April 11, 2002
Copyright: 2002 The Cincinnati Enquirer

The nation's drug czar on Wednesday unveiled a new tool in the war against alcohol and other drugs - patriotism.

(MarijuanaNews note: " Alcohol and other drugs? " This should be a warning to the alcohol industry. However, as we will see, it is really still all about cannabis.)

See
Drug Czar's Comments On Drug Survey of Young Children
Show That The " War on Drugs " Is Really Just A War On Marijuana

John Walters, director of the Office of National Drug Control Policy, told the Pride World Drug Prevention Conference that illegal drug trafficking is helping fund at least 12 terrorist groups.

" Drugs are not only dangerous for you and your friends, " he said. " It's bad for your country and bad for people who want to live in peace and democracy. "

(MarijuanaNews note: Hyper-lie number one, trying to link " drugs " with terrorism.

Falsely invoking patriotism has been called the last refuge of scoundrels, and Walters is the sort of person who gives scoundrels a bad name. Half of all the cannabis consumed in DEAland is grown there and the rest comes from Mexico and a few other countries. And of course, whatever connection there might be to " terrorism " is inherent in prohibition, not the substances.

Then he talks about " peace and democracy? " This from an Administration that is waging war on the sick and dying, while ignoring overwhelming popular support for medical cannabis.)


Mr. Walters spoke to 4,500 teens and adults attending the opening day of the four-day conference at the Albert B. Sabin Cincinnati Convention Center. Pride, the sponsoring organization, takes its name from the acronym for Parents' Resource Institute for Drug Education.

The 25th anniversary event provides training to prevent use of tobacco, alcohol and illegal drugs among adolescents.

(MarijuanaNews note: One year when I was National Director of NORML, I happened to be in Cincinnati at the same time as the PRIDE conference [My invitation to present an alternative view must have gotten lost in the mail.]

I walked past the conference center just as the kids were coming out. I did not identify myself, because I just wanted to find out what they were being told.

I have two memories of short conversations with the teens, one sad, one comical.

I have a very sad memory of a very sweet looking girl about 14, well-dressed, her teeth in braces. She told me that she would rather live in a totalitarian country than in one where cannabis was legal. I wonder what she thinks today now that she is an adult.

On a lighter note, a boy about the same age told me that one of the signs of marijuana use is a green tongue. Really, that is still a part of prohibitionist propaganda.

By the most wonderful of coincidences I had just had a green breath mint. So I opened my mouth and asked, " like this? " I thought he was going to do a back-flip!

Oh yes, then there was the kid who said nothing but grinned when he showed me a cannabis leaf he had drawn on the under side of his baseball cap bill! If Chairman Mao couldn't brainwash the Chinese people in a totalitarian society the prohibitionists cannot brainwash American kids in the age of the Internet, even with the help of the Cincinnati Enquirer.)

As drug czar, Mr. Walters promises to reduce drug use among adults and teens by 10 percent in two years and by 25 percent in five years.

(MarijuanaNews note: What nonsense! And to better understand the absurdity of this " promise " consider that the statistics on both licit and illicit substance use are completely unreliable --- plus there is an almost five point margin of error in the survey numbers. This means that there could be no real change and yet report almost a ten point increase or decrease. Oh, and will Walters resign if he does not keep his " promise? "

See

Then remember that DEAland was supposed to be " drug-free " 10 years ago, according to an act of Congress.)

" It begins with prevention, " he said. " We know if you don't become involved in drug use as a teenager, you're very unlikely to have abuse or addiction problems later. "

Today, an estimated 4.7 million people are drug-dependent. Of those, 23 percent are estimated to be teenagers.

(MarijuanaNews note: Now for hyper-lie number two, a new entry into " the media will repeat any lie we tell " game.

There is a progression of lies here. This article began with a reference to " alcohol and other drugs " and talked about " training to prevent use of tobacco, alcohol and illegal drugs among adolescents. "

So that is the context that they set.

Last month, over 50 million Americans smoked tobacco last month, and most of them are " addicted, " and over 100 million Americans drank alcohol. The National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism says about 14 million of them are " alcoholic or abuse alcohol. " The institute also says 53 percent of adult Americans say they have a close relative with a " drinking problem. "

Between 20 percent and 30 percent of patients in emergency rooms have alcohol problems, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Nearly half of alcohol-related deaths are the result of motor-vehicle crashes, falls, fires, drowning, homicides and suicides.

According to a study published on April 9th by the National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism, drinking kills 1,400 college students every year and plays a role in 70,000 cases of sexual assault and date rape on campus. It also said that a quarter of all U.S. college students have driven under the influence of alcohol, and 500,000 have been injured because of alcohol.

Meanwhile John Walters is saving the kids from cannabis.. )

Marijuana is the most misunderstood drug, Mr. Walters said, because it's peddled as harmless.

See

Sixty-five percent of drug-dependent people have a primary or secondary dependence on marijuana.

" Marijuana is two-thirds of the addiction problem in America today .

(MarijuanaNews note: How did marijuana become " two-thirds of the addiction problem in America today? "

Easy.

First, despite the stated context, ignore all addictions to legal drugs, which vastly exceed the total number " addicted " to all illegal drugs combined, and never mind prescription drug addiction which is another story entirely. Then define any use of an illegal drug as abuse, therefore someone who is addicted to alcohol, heroin or cocaine, etc. has " secondary dependence " on marijuana, the most widely used illicit substance, by far.

Thus " Marijuana is two-thirds of the addiction problem in America today .... " Simple!

Now what are the facts?

Last December, a report by the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration,

The numbers came from the latest " Treatment Episode Data Set, " which tracks DEAland admissions to state-approved facilities for substance abuse treatment. These centers see an estimated 1.6 million admissions each year.

The rehab business is huge, and unfortunately it is so politicized that the part that deals with illicit substances, especially cannabis, is often just a racket.

This survey, which covered 1.6 million cases of adults and youths over age 12 who were admitted for treatment at a center, found that most were abusing alcohol -- 47 percent.

Sixteen percent were users of opiates, mostly heroin, 14 percent used cocaine and 14 percent marijuana or hashish.

It said that more than half the patients " abused " more than one substance. Remember, any use of an illegal substance is called " abuse " in the prohibitionist lexicon.

This is the first link in Walters chain of lies.

Here is the second:

In 1994, 43 percent of teens " treated for substance abuse " were marijuana users. In 1999, 60 percent were. " Marijuana admissions " rose in many states, with the overall rate for teens and adults climbing from 69 per 100,000 people in 1994 to 103 per 100,000 in 1999. This mirrors the increase in marijuana arrests under Clinton, and the increase in employer urine testing, which is primarily aimed at cannabis users. Employees who fail urine tests are often required to get " treatment " in order to keep their jobs.

According to the report, half of them were sent to treatment by the courts.

See

So when prohibition, meaning the courts and mandatory urine testing, forces people who do not need treatment into the hands of the rehab racketeers, this not only wastes badly needed treatment funding, it is also used to justify more arrests and more urine testing for marijuana users. And so it goes. Then, John Walters can say, " While we can all be thankful that people who need help are getting it, this report shows some of the real-life consequences of marijuana use.''

No, it shows the real-life consequences of cannabis prohibition, but the media cannot use the word " prohibition " except to refer to 1920s alcohol policies. Don't even think about it.)

The conference, which continues through Saturday, will bring $4.2 million into the local economy.

(MarijuanaNews note: Now try to understand the broader implications of taking lying to new levels, which I call hyper-lying

Theodore Dalrymple, the British physician and columnist, writing in a different but related context, echoed Orwell when he described such lying:

" The point of such propaganda is not to persuade, much less to inform: it is to humiliate and to render docile. The more at variance the tenor of the propaganda is with everyday reality, the more impotent the recipient feels, and the more firmly in the grip of a giant organisation against which all resistance is futile. "

The children are mere props for Walters operation on the media. Here a major metropolitan newspaper is dragged down even further into the war on meaning, the war on freedom and the war on the sick and dying. Almost all papers would have responded in exactly the same way. As they become ever more involved, they have an even greater investment in the war itself. It's not the crime; it's the cover-up. Then, the cover-up becomes the crime.

How can they explain their own actions to their readers? They cannot, and so it goes.)
